31.0.0.en: Laban's sons were troubled when they saw Jacob growing richer than their father, and they spoke with their father about this, so he too was troubled by Jacob and no longer treated him with love, and Jacob understood this.

31.0.1.en: Do not be troubled by the advancement of those around you and do not compare yourself with them, and if you see their advancement and want to be like them, ask God and wish them good, and God will give to you and to them.

31.1.0.en: God strengthened Jacob, who felt his estrangement among Laban and his sons and longed to return to the land of Canaan, by appearing to him and commanding him to return.

31.2.0.en: Jacob summoned his two wives, Leah and Rachel, to the field where he was working at shepherding, far from the eyes and ears of the servants, to speak with them about the decision to depart, and told them of the change in Laban's treatment of him because of God's blessing on his possessions, although he had served Laban with all his strength and great faithfulness for twenty years, including the fourteen years of the dowry and then six years working for wages with him. He mentioned to them how he had borne the bad treatment of their father, who changed his wages ten times during the six years in which he had fixed wages for him: sometimes he would say to him that your wages are the striped sheep, and when these striped sheep increased with him, he would return and say to him, from now on your wages are the black sheep ... and so on. Thus Laban wanted to take the best for himself, while on the contrary God was blessing Jacob in his sheep so they increased. By this blessing of God, God took away Laban's strength and wealth and gave it to Jacob.

31.3.0.en: Ringstraked: its skin is mottled like the skin of a leopard, with black and white spots.

31.3.1.en: Jacob informed his two wives of a divine dream he had seen: at the time of the mating of the sheep he saw the rams, striped, spotted and speckled, mounting the ewes to mate in order to produce mottled sheep, and God said to him, I am the one who blessed your work so that your wealth in sheep might increase. He reminded him of His promise to him, when He appeared to him on the ladder in the dream at Bethel, to bless him, when he poured oil on the stone, and then commanded him to leave Laban and return to Canaan, so Jacob was reassured by the blessing of God that was with him. This vision declares the blessing of God that was with Jacob, and perhaps it was He who guided him to place the rods in the watering troughs, and it answers everyone who accuses Jacob of trickery and deceit. For it was God who guided him to that in order to rescue him from Laban's greed in changing his wages and exploiting him in every way.

31.3.2.en: In proportion to the tribulations that pass over you, God reveals Himself to you and supports you, and the more you are submissive to Him, He directs you in all your steps, so you advance successfully however great the difficulties around you.

31.4.0.en: Leah and Rachel showed their distress at their father's greed, for he sold them in their marriage and received the price, which was Jacob's work of 14 years, and he did not give them many gifts as Bethuel, Laban's father, gave his daughter Rebekah at her marriage. Thus they lost all inheritance of their own from their father, and he counted them as strangers, and they felt that the wealth that God had transferred from Laban to Jacob was a recovery of their share taken away from their father's house. Thus they showed their support for Jacob and their readiness to depart with him and obey God's commands.

31.4.1.en: When you submit to God and walk with Him, He makes your way easy and makes those around you agree with you and submit to you, so you are not hindered in your spiritual growth and the carrying out of God's will.

31.5.0.en: God arranged that Laban should be busy shearing his sheep, and the days of shearing are days of joy because he gathers much money from the sale of the sheared wool, so Laban and all with him were busy with the shearing. Jacob seized this opportunity and gathered his wives, his children and his servants and mounted them, and likewise all his possessions, and set out with them and crossed the Euphrates River heading to the land of Canaan, that is, the land that God had promised to give him as an inheritance, where his father Isaac lived, and headed to the region of Gilead, which lies east of the Jordan River in Canaan.

31.5.1.en: Rachel did a strange and unexpected thing: she stole some of her father's idol images and departed with them with Jacob, and this was for one of the following reasons:

31.5.2.en: 1- Either to exploit their material value in silver or gold, out of distress at her father's greed and his exploitation of them.

31.5.3.en: 2- Or because of some attachment in her heart to the worship of idols, in which these images were used to seek counsel, protection and good omens, although she had lived in the faith with Jacob for many years.

31.6.0.en: Laban discovered after three days that Jacob had left the place, and he did not discover it at once because of his busyness with the shearing of the sheep, and he also noticed the theft of his images. So he gathered his brethren, meaning his relatives, and his sons and his mighty men, and pursued Jacob until he overtook him after seven days, that is, after a journey of about 100 miles, in Mount Gilead, which lies east of the Jordan River. When he saw Jacob and those with him from afar, Laban pitched his tents at the mountain.

31.7.0.en: Laban reached Jacob with strong men who could have taken away his children and possessions, but God, who protects Jacob, appeared to Laban and warned him against harming Jacob by any word or action.

31.7.1.en: Your God is strong and able to do all things, so do not be troubled if the wicked surround you and threaten you or wrong you, for He protects you and rescues you from their hands and troubles them, and even turns their wrongs to your spiritual benefit.

31.8.0.en: Each party saw the other's tents beside Mount Gilead, and Laban did not advance to harm Jacob after God's command to him.

31.9.0.en: Captives taken with the sword: the prisoners whom the enemy seizes in war.

31.9.1.en: The tabret: now called the riq, a wooden frame over which skin is stretched and to which cymbals are attached that make a strong sound when the skin is struck.

31.9.3.en: Laban reproached Jacob for his flight and for taking his daughters like captives fleeing in secret, and because he deprived him of bidding farewell to his daughters and grandchildren and kissing them, and did not give him the opportunity to hold a farewell celebration and a procession with songs and musical instruments.

31.10.1.en: Laban admitted that he had been determined to harm Jacob, relying on the strength of the men who were with him, but on the previous day God had appeared to him and warned him against harming Jacob.

31.11.0.en: Laban reproached Jacob because he had stolen his images and said to him, You longed to see your father, so why did you steal my gods?

31.12.0.en: Jacob justified his flight by his fear that Laban would take his daughters, that is, Jacob's wives, from him. As for the theft of the images, he denied it completely, because he did not know what Rachel had done, and therefore said, Search all my tents, and with whomever you find the images, let him be put to death, or become your slave, or not live a normal life because he sinned by this theft.

31.13.0.en: The camel's furniture: what is placed on the camel for a person to ride on, with large pockets in which belongings are put.

31.13.1.en: Laban went in to search the tents himself, and did not find them in any of the tents, not even Rachel's tent, because when he entered it she had put the images in the camel's furniture and sat on top of them, and excused herself to her father by her weariness from the pains of the monthly period that comes to women. He searched with his hand all through the tent and did not find them ... Thus the sin of stealing led Rachel to lying also, but God, for the sake of the wronged Jacob, covered her and did not reveal her sin.

31.13.2.en: Beware of being lax with sin, and if you sin, hasten to repentance, lest it lead you to other sins; on the contrary, care to acquire virtues, for just as the virtues are a chain in which each leads to the other, so also sins are a chain in which each leads to the other.

31.14.0.en: You have hotly pursued after me: you hastened after me impetuously to harm me.

31.14.1.en: Jacob reproached Laban for pursuing him to harm him and for this false accusation of theft, and even demanded that he bring the stolen things as evidence of the accusation and place them before his men who had come with him, to prove his accusation, otherwise let it be enough of wronging him.

31.15.0.en: He reminded him of his faithfulness in tending his sheep and keeping them for 20 years, so why did he wrong him and harm him despite this faithfulness, when he had not stolen from him a single sheep?

31.16.0.en: Of Jacob's faithfulness, and even his self-giving, was that he would make good to Laban any sheep that one of the wild beasts tore, although the owner of the sheep should have borne what was torn, but in order not to enter into dispute with the greedy Laban, he bore any loss that occurred, whether an animal tore it or a thief stole it.

31.17.0.en: Jacob bore the hardships of shepherding by day and by night, enduring the heat of the day and the cold of the night, which sometimes reaches the falling of rain and ice. And because of his care for the flocks he sometimes stayed up all night thinking how to manage and tend them.

31.18.0.en: Jacob reminded Laban how he had tried to exploit him throughout his service to him of twenty years and how he had changed his wages ten times in the last six years, the meaning being not the number ten but many times, and Jacob bore this and remained faithful in his service.

31.19.0.en: Jacob showed Laban's injustice and greed throughout his stay with him, and none rescued him and his possessions from his hands except God, who had promised Abraham and Isaac blessing, and out of respect for Isaac, the husband of his sister Rebekah, who was still alive. And the power of God appeared in warning and rebuking Laban against harming Jacob.

31.19.1.en: Be faithful in bearing your responsibilities and your service to God, whatever the faults of others, for He will keep you and protect you and bless your life.

31.20.0.en: Laban said to Jacob, Your wives and children are my children and your sheep also are dear to me because they are the offspring of my sheep, so we are united and all your possessions are dear to me, and therefore the natural situation is that neither of us should harm the other. Come, let us make a covenant of peace and a pact that neither of us will hurt the other all our lives.

31.21.0.en: Jegar-sahadutha: in Syriac, and its meaning is the heap of witness.

31.21.1.en: Galeed: in Hebrew, and its meaning is also the heap of witness.

31.21.2.en: Mizpah: its meaning is the watchtower.

31.21.3.en: Jacob agreed to Laban's word because he was a peaceable man, so he took a stone and set it up in the middle and asked the men who were with Laban to gather stones around this stone, and they made a heap, that is, a pile of stones, and then ate upon it to declare their love and reconciliation. They called it the heap of witness because it bears witness to the peace between them, and they also called it the watchtower because God watches over this covenant so that no one will violate it. The heap of witness is a type of the Cross, and the food that they ate is a type of the sacrament of Holy Communion.

31.22.0.en: Laban declared that this covenant meant keeping Jacob's wives, who were Laban's daughters, so that he would not marry other women and humiliate Leah and Rachel, and that neither party would move and pass beyond this heap to harm the other.

31.23.0.en: Laban swore by his gods and the God of Abraham, while Jacob called himself to witness by the fear and honor of his father Isaac, which he had received from God. This means that Laban was still worshiping idols and considered the God of Abraham one of the gods, while Isaac and Jacob worshiped God alone.

31.24.0.en: Jacob offered sacrifices to confirm the covenant and they ate together as proof of love, and then Laban and his men departed, returning to their country.

31.24.1.en: How beautiful is reconciliation between you and all people! Seek it however much others wrong you, that you may keep your peace and go on to your goal, which is the love of God, and be free for every positive work.

32.0.0.en: Jacob was thinking about meeting his brother Esau, and whether he would accept meeting him or refuse, or try to take revenge on him for what he had done to him 20 years before when he stole his blessing. Therefore God reassured him through his meeting with Laban, for God appeared and prevented Laban from harming him and a treaty of peace was made. And now He reassures him a second time after he set out toward his brother to meet him, for a company of angels appeared to him, as one appeared to him in the past when he fled from Esau in the dream of the ladder, to confirm to him that He had not forgotten His promise to keep him as long as he held fast to his faith.

32.1.0.en: Mahanaim: it lies east of the Jordan River at about its middle, between it and the Jabbok River, which branches off from about its middle toward the east and runs to the north.

32.1.1.en: When Jacob saw the angels he rejoiced greatly and said, This is God's host, and his heart was reassured, and he called the name of the place where they appeared to him Mahanaim, that is, two camps, meaning the camp or host of the angels in heaven and God's camp on earth, which is Jacob and his family. For the Church consists of a part in heaven and a part still striving on earth.

32.1.2.en: God cares for your feelings as long as you seek Him and want to live with Him, and He moves toward you and shows you His love in many forms to reassure you, so enjoy Him and thank Him, and move on your way in life leaning on His hand.

32.2.0.en: The land of Seir: Seir means hairy, and the land of Seir is a mountain range that extends from the Gulf of Aqaba to the Dead Sea.

32.2.1.en: Edom: the meaning is red, and what is meant by it is the offspring of Esau, which lives in the land of Seir, which had belonged to the Horites, and the offspring of Esau took possession of it from them.

32.2.2.en: Despite God's reassurance to Jacob, there was still within him a fear of Esau's revenge on him, so he sent messengers from his servants to Esau to learn his feelings toward him, and the messengers went south along the Jordan River and the Dead Sea until they reached the mountains of Seir. In this he depended on his human thinking and did not consult God.

32.2.3.en: If there is anxiety or fear within you, take refuge in God many times, and do not rush in your anxiety to take decisions that you think will protect you but that in truth increase your anxiety and may harm you. Seek God, for He is near you and will guide you to your good.

32.3.0.en: Jacob gave his messengers a message to Esau, full of humility and fear and also carrying meanings of love, and told him in it that he had lived abroad 20 years with his uncle Laban and God had blessed him with many servants and cattle, and he was returning to Canaan and hoped to find grace and acceptance in his eyes. His humility appears from his calling him my lord, although they were brothers, indeed Jacob had received from God authority over his brother as a blessing from Isaac.

32.4.0.en: The messengers informed Esau of this message, and they found him very rich, and when he heard it he went out with 400 men of his servants to meet Jacob. This means one of two things:

32.4.1.en: 1- Either joy and welcome at meeting his brother.

32.4.2.en: 2- Or preparation for revenge because of his being deprived of his father's blessing.

32.4.3.en: Esau had decided to take revenge on his brother, but after the death of their father ... so is he still insisting on revenge? ... And will he take revenge now or postpone it until after Isaac's death? ... Or has he calmed down and forgotten what happened after God blessed him with many offspring and servants? We cannot know, and perhaps feelings of longing for his brother were mixed with feelings of revenge and distress; in any case, the hope is in God's intervention to reconcile the two brothers.

32.5.0.en: When Jacob heard from his messengers the news of Esau's coming out with his many men to meet him, he was very afraid, remembering the decision of revenge that Esau had declared 20 years before ... Thus Jacob did not benefit from relying on his own thinking and sending messengers, but his fear increased, so he divided those who were with him into two companies and separated them, so that if Esau attacked one company the other would find an opportunity to flee.

32.6.0.en: After Jacob's human attempts failed, he took refuge in God. The text of his prayer is mentioned here, and it is the first prayer in the Holy Bible whose text is given, and it includes many meanings, the most important of which are:

32.6.1.en: 1- His sense of sonship to God and his special relationship with Him, since he calls Him the God of his fathers, and this makes him speak with boldness and confidence.

32.6.2.en: 2- He declares his submission to God's commands, who commanded him to return from Haran to Canaan, and by this he affirms his allegiance to God and his taking refuge in Him.

32.7.0.en: 3- He declares in humility his unworthiness of the kindness and blessings of God that He had given him ... Thus boldness and confidence in God are mingled with deep humility.

32.7.1.en: 4- He thanks God and declares that He is the source of all the favor and blessing upon him, because when he fled from Esau and crossed the Jordan River on his way to Haran he possessed nothing at all. And after his return from Haran to Canaan God blessed him, so he became two hosts, that is, two companies, including his wives, children, servants and possessions, so in himself he is nothing, but God's blessing made him very great.

32.8.0.en: The mother with the children: he means his wives and children.

32.8.1.en: 5- He asked God to rescue him from the hand of his brother Esau, who was coming to take revenge on him, because if God did not intervene he would kill all who were with him, the great and the small.

32.9.0.en: 6- He reminded God of His promises to him of blessing and many offspring. And God rejoices in His children who hold fast to His promises and remind Him of them, that is, ask Him to care for them.

32.9.1.en: Show your feelings to God in love and humility and ask of Him what you want, for He is your heavenly Father who loves you and rejoices in your words and supports you whatever your weakness, indeed your few words are very precious to Him.

32.10.0.en: Jacob rested part of the night and thought during it of sending gifts to his brother Esau, to soften his heart toward him and establish friendly relations with him that would make him forget feelings of distress and revenge.

32.10.1.en: Do not be troubled by feelings of evil if they surround you, and know that love is stronger than hatred, so pray for those who oppose you and offer them love in kind words or gifts or services, even if they do not welcome it at first, but they are gradually affected by it, so you remove the evil from their hearts and keep your peace and win the hearts of many. This is not weakness, but it is true strength, to change people's hearts from evil to good, and do not care about what they say about you at first, that you are weak or that they think of exploiting you, for you are the stronger by your love and you please God, who supports you and subdues them to you and blesses your life.

32.11.0.en: She-camel: the female of the camel.

32.11.1.en: He-goat: the male of the goat.

32.11.2.en: She-ass: the female of the donkey.

32.11.3.en: Ewe: the female of the sheep.

32.11.4.en: She-goat: the female of the goat.

32.11.5.en: Ram: the male of the sheep.

32.11.6.en: The details of the gift sent to Esau are mentioned, a group of herds of cattle numbering 580 head, which is a great gift and means two things:

32.11.8.en: 2- His great love and his fear of Esau and his attempt to appease him.

32.12.1.en: He divided the gift into a group of gifts, giving each drove to some of his servants, probably dividing it into five droves, and put a sufficient distance between each drove and the next so that it would clearly appear that they were five gifts, so they would gradually affect Esau's heart and absorb all the anger within him.

32.13.0.en: He charged his servants who led the droves that when each of them met Esau and he asked him who he was and what was with him, he should say to him, It is a present sent from your servant Jacob. And he said within himself, By this I will appease him and gain his favor before I meet him.

32.14.0.en: Jacob sent his gift ahead of him to Esau, while he himself lodged or rested part of the night in the place where he had pitched his tent.

32.15.0.en: Ford: a part of the river of little depth that can be crossed on foot, and the width of the river is small in this region.

32.15.1.en: Jabbok: one of the tributaries of the Jordan River, branching off from about its middle, as we mentioned, at a distance of 23 miles north of the Dead Sea, and the meaning of its name is the flowing, and it is now called the Zarqa.

32.15.2.en: The gift crossed with his servants to Esau, then the rest of his servants with all his possessions crossed the Jabbok River heading south toward the Dead Sea, and only his wives and children remained with Jacob, so he crossed with them the Jabbok River on foot, heading south as a caravan before him, while he himself remained alone for the rest of the night.

32.16.0.en: The hollow of his thigh: the place where the thigh joins the body.

32.16.1.en: After the caravan of his wives and children had gone some distance on their way to meet Esau, and this was during the night, Jacob remained alone and stood praying, asking God's help in his meeting with Esau, that He would turn away his anger and that he would not take revenge on him. While he was praying, God wished to reassure him, so He appeared to him in the form of an angel or sent him an angel in human form, and Jacob felt that he was a heavenly being, so he hastened to hold him and ask his help. The angel pretended that he wanted to depart from him, but Jacob clung to him asking his blessing because he felt that he was sent from God. Jacob continued to implore him, clinging to him, through the rest of the night until the dawn rose, and the angel pretended weakness before Jacob as if unable to free himself from his clinging, in order to encourage him as he continued to ask his blessing and help, and Jacob even says to him, "I will not let thee go, except thou bless me," for I am in great need before the power of Esau who is coming against me. In the end the angel not only blessed him but struck him, that is, touched him, on the hollow of his thigh, so the thigh was partly dislocated from the body, and Jacob suffered pain but continued to hold the angel, asking his help. This shows how much Jacob clung to God and his sense of his weakness and need.

32.16.2.en: Strive in your prayers with God and ask Him for all you want. Be persistent with Him, declaring your need with the boldness of sons, for He rejoices in your faith and your clinging to Him, and when He sees the extent of your striving He will surely give you many blessings. Do not doubt or despair, and hold fast to God.

32.17.0.en: The angel changed Jacob's name to Israel, which means he wrestles with God, in honor of Jacob because of his spiritual striving in prayer and his faith and reliance on Him, and on the other hand because of his bearing with others such as Laban until God blessed him and enriched him and sent him away from him in peace. By this he is an example for all his offspring in holding fast to God and in good dealing with others, because his offspring were called by this name, that is, the children of Israel.

32.18.0.en: Jacob asked the angel, or the spiritual person who appeared to him, about his name, and he did not answer him, because he had understood that he was a spiritual being from heaven, and he gave him what he needed, which was the blessing, and then ascended from him.

32.19.0.en: Peniel or Penuel: the meaning is the face of God.

32.19.1.en: Jacob rejoiced with an inexpressible joy because he had seen God and felt His presence through his meeting with the angel, so he called the name of the place Peniel.

32.20.0.en: In the morning, when the sun rose, Jacob was reassured and moved south to catch up with his wives and children, and he was suffering from the angel's blow, so he limped in his walking. God permitted him this pain throughout his life so that he would not be proud because of his vision and his wrestling with God, but would always feel his weakness and need, and so continue to enjoy God's work with him. And the offspring of Jacob magnified this great event in the life of their father, so they did not eat the sinew of the thigh, which is the nerve extending along the leg, in esteem and reverence for this great event, that is, Jacob's meeting with God, which resulted in the pain apparent in his walking.

32.20.1.en: The meeting with Esau and settling in Canaan
